lines: You finished the class. Now see what changed.
End the ride, and Wattzup saves it and opens its summary.
Average power leads, with the change since last time.
Every cadence dip is marked on the trace.
Point at a dip in the list, and its band lights up.
Beside it, your streak, this week's rides, and any best you set.
Progress compares a class you have ridden more than once.
Average power, cadence on target, or dips, attempt by attempt.
Every saved ride is listed, with six weeks of streak and your achievements.
On a phone, the summary and progress stack into one column.
What the tests prove: a bike ride of a minute or more is saved, and kept after a restart.
Streaks and bests come from your own rides, never invented.
That is journey fourteen. Wattzup turns an Echelon bike or treadmill into a live training display.
